name: Carrion Defense Works Pathogen Delivery System PDS-4 'Typhoid'
description: A weapon system designed to deliver engineered biological agents via aerosolized capsules launched from a modified grenade launcher platform. The PDS-4 fires capsules that burst on impact, releasing clouds of pathogen-carrying particles calibrated for maximum infection rate through respiratory exposure. Carrion offers a range of pathogen payloads — from fast-acting incapacitants that simulate severe flu symptoms to slow-developing agents designed for covert population-level delivery. The system exists in a legal gray zone: Carrion officially markets the launcher for 'agricultural pest control aerosol delivery,' and the pathogen payloads are sold through separate, deniable supply chains.
legality: Prohibited — biological weapon (officially does not exist as weapon)
specifications:
launcher type: Modified 40mm grenade platform
effective range: 30-100 meters
aerosolization radius: 8 meters from impact
pathogen options: Fast incapacitant, slow-develop covert, targeted genetic-marker selective
infection rate: 85-95% for unprotected respiratory exposure
capsule weight: 0.2 kg
magazine: 6 capsules
launcher weight: 3.8 kg
countermeasure: NBC-grade respiratory filtration
story_hooks: A mystery illness spreading through Tier 2 has been traced to PDS-4 capsule fragments found in ventilation systems — someone deployed a slow-acting pathogen and the infection is still spreading.
Carrion's genetic-marker-selective pathogen has been loaded into PDS-4 capsules — it only affects people with a specific genetic heritage, making it an instrument of ethnic targeting.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist, utilitarian launcher built on a modified 40mm grenade platform. The body is compact and angular, designed for single-handed operation with a pronounced curve at the breech. The aesthetic is deliberately clinical and unmarked — no flash, no ornamentation. It reads as a tool engineered for quiet, deniable work.
physical_description.dimensions: 48 cm length, 12 cm width at widest point (magazine housing), 8 cm height. Barrel: 15 cm. 6-capsule rotary magazine extends 6 cm below frame.
physical_description.weight_description: Deceptively light at 3.8 kg — feels almost fragile until you feel the density in the lower receiver. Balanced toward the breech. The capsules themselves are nearly weightless, which contributes to an unsettling impression of lethality without mass.
physical_description.primary_material: Reinforced polymer composite (likely polyetheretherketone or equivalent) for the frame and grip. Stainless steel breech block and barrel. Titanium capsule magazine housing.
physical_description.finish: Matte gray-black polymer, weathered to a dull charcoal. The metal components are brushed stainless — no shine, no reflection. Deliberately designed not to catch light. Surface shows micro-scratches consistent with field use and intentional wear-marking to defeat recognition patterns.
physical_description.color_scheme: Slate gray primary body, dull steel accents. No branding colors. Capsules themselves appear as translucent or frosted amber tubes, contents invisible.
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow checkering — designed for gloved operation. Slightly tacky, non-slip surface. The trigger guard is oversized, accommodating reinforced tactical gloves.
distinctive_features: Unmarked rotary magazine with numbered capsule positions (1-6) in faint gray laser etching
Breech block features a tiny pressure-relief vent disguised as manufacturing artifact
Barrel has microscopic rifling-like grooves to ensure capsule spin for aerosol dispersal pattern optimization
No sights — designed for point-and-fire use at close range
Magazine release is a concealed push-button on the grip, not a lever
Muzzle opening is slightly flared, optimized for capsule burst dispersal cone rather than ballistic accuracy
Serial number etched in near-invisible nano-scale characters on the lower receiver
Faint stress fractures in polymer suggest previous use without maintenance logs
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: No visible Carrion Defense Works logo or branding anywhere. A single laser-etched line under the barrel reads 'AGRICULTURAL DISPERSAL UNIT' with a six-digit code. This is plausible deniability: the official designation obscures the weapon's true function.
physical_description.condition_typical: Well-maintained but deliberately worn. No dirt or corrosion, but surface shows deliberate marking and scuffing to avoid pattern-recognition systems. Capsule magazines show slight oxidation on the metal housing, suggesting field storage in humid conditions. The launcher itself is operational and clean, but gives the impression of being used sporadically and covertly rather than regularly drilled.
